text: {"lessons":["Selling Stock B for a gain and later buying it back—and selling again before its price rose further—reminds me not to anchor on my purchase price or rush to lock in gains; I should judge each trade by its prospective risk and return.","A loss feels especially painful, and I dislike admitting mistakes, but neither my average cost nor my feelings justify holding a stock; I should reassess it objectively against my other holdings.","My account value has moved sharply even when I made no trades, and past price changes do not predict future ones; I should avoid reactive trading and keep diversification and total portfolio risk in view."]}
